name: Welltower
description: Welltower owns senior-housing, wellness-housing and post-acute properties, mostly in the U.S., Canada and the U.K., and reports three segments: Seniors Housing Operating, Triple-net and Outpatient Medical. In Seniors Housing Operating it owns the buildings and is paid directly by residents (monthly fees for rent, meals and care), while 62 operating partners run the communities for an incentive-based management fee; Welltower keeps the net operating income and carries the occupancy and cost risk. In Triple-net it leases properties to operators under long leases, and in Outpatient Medical it leases medical office buildings to health-care tenants. Revenue grew 36 percent in FY2025 to $10.84 billion on acquisitions (including Barchester in the U.K. in October 2025) while it sold a large block of outpatient medical properties.

gics.note: Conventional label recorded from general knowledge of the standard scheme; not re-checked against an MSCI/S&P source in this pass. SEC SIC code is 6798 (Real Estate Investment Trusts). The box misleads on the largest line: 78 percent of FY2025 revenue was resident fees and services from Seniors Housing Operating properties, which Welltower owns and whose whole operating result (revenue less about $6.2B of property costs) it bears, with third-party managers paid a management fee. That is closer to owning a senior-living operating business than to a landlord collecting rent, and it means profit swings with occupancy and wages rather than with a fixed lease.

employees.note: 712 employees at Dec 31, 2025 (10-K); the communities themselves are staffed by its operating partners, not by Welltower

businessLines.name: Seniors Housing Operating
businessLines.how: Residents pay monthly fees (rent plus meals and care services) that Welltower books as revenue; it pays the operating partner a management fee with an incentive component and pays all property operating costs, so income depends on occupancy, rate increases and operating cost growth.
businessLines.description: Independent living, assisted living, memory care, continuing care retirement communities, wellness housing and U.K. care homes, mostly held through the RIDEA structure and run by operating partners (62 at Dec 31, 2025).

revenue.note: +40.7% vs $6,035.5M FY2024 (10-K: 78% of total revenues, 76% in 2024, 72% in 2023). Includes resident fees and services $8,453.0M plus other income $36.1M

businessLines.revenueNote: +40.7% vs $6,035.5M FY2024 (10-K: 78% of total revenues, 76% in 2024, 72% in 2023). Includes resident fees and services $8,453.0M plus other income $36.1M

operatingProfit.note: Consolidated NOI: revenue less property operating expenses of $6,199.6M; FY2024 NOI $1,511.7M

businessLines.name: Triple-net
businessLines.how: The operator pays contractual rent (usually with escalators) and covers the property's operating costs and taxes; Welltower has almost no operating cost, hence a 97% NOI margin, but rent coverage depends on the operator's health.
businessLines.description: Seniors housing and post-acute properties leased to operators under long-term leases. The largest relationship is Integra Healthcare Properties (about 16% of Triple-net revenues and 2% of total).

businessLines.name: Outpatient Medical
businessLines.how: Tenants pay rent under non-cancellable operating leases (weighted-average remaining term eight years at Dec 31, 2025), often backed by security deposits, guarantees or letters of credit; the 10-K says 24% of leases are partial expense-reimbursement (modified gross) and 10% are gross with no reimbursement, the rest passing more expenses to the tenant.
businessLines.description: Medical office and outpatient buildings leased to health systems and physician groups. Welltower has been selling a large block: 241 properties for $5,224.9M total sale price were disposed of by Dec 31, 2025 under a definitive agreement (gain $881.4M, including $663.8M of non-cash consideration in a retained mandatorily redeemable preferred interest).
